newsitem.title: CHINA: China interbank market rates (CHIBOR) mostly up.
newsitem.headline: China interbank market rates (CHIBOR) mostly up.

text.p: Following is the China Interbank Offered Rate (CHIBOR) for Tuesday, issued by the official Xinhua news agency on behalf of the People's Bank of China, the central bank.
The figures represent weighted averages and not closing prices and they are annual percentage rates.
The central bank does not post volumes.
Traders said trading was dull today with market sentiment continuing to be weak despite the rises in the rates.

They said the market was dominated by negative factors including the increasingly low anti-inflationary subsidy paid for long-term treasury bonds and bank deposits. The market expects the subsidy to be completely abolished by end-1996.
"Sentiment was weakened by the negative factors," one trader said. "Also, there is sufficient money supply on the market."
"The market was dull and directionless with the exception of institutional speculation," a second trader said. "They borrow here and lend at higher rates on the T-bill repurchase market."
